subject.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `message_pre_auth` / `message:pre-auth` as a supported pre-admission hook that can expose blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DM content to trusted handlers, along with grouped DM allowlist metadata as a config and plugin contract?
rationale: Automation can fix the known-event registry gap, but the permanent privacy, plugin API, config, CLI, and hook auto-loading contract is a maintainer security/product decision.

options.title: Sponsor After Registry Fix
options.body: Accept the feature direction after adding `message:pre-auth` to the known internal event registry and confirming the trust-boundary documentation and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pause For Shared Audit Contract
options.body: Hold this PR until denied-inbound audit work defines redaction, retention, rate limiting, and notification semantics across channels.

options.title: Narrow To External Hook Package
options.body: Decline core pre-auth exposure for now and ask for a ClawHub/plugin-style access-request package once a smaller supported extension seam exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor After Registry Fix
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction after adding `message:pre-auth` to the known internal event registry and confirming the trust-boundary documentation and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared ingress, plugin SDK/config contracts, and security-sensitive channel behavior where recent history points to steipete as an adjacent owner.
